BLUEPRINT_CONFLICT AGAINST MY OWN PREVIOUS FINDING - and the previous finding was wrong.

The last round rejected this option partly for having 'lost its wedge taper', claiming the drawing shows a flap 2.3:1 deeper at the inner end. This grader extracted the red guide mark BY COLOUR and profiled its vertical extent column by column: wearer's-left mark x=699-857 with extents 85,85,85,82,82,84,85,80,82,82; wearer's-right x=333-490 with extents 81,84,82,80,84,82,81,85,84,86. Top edge 23.2 degrees, bottom edge 22.2. THE DRAWN FLAP IS A PARALLELOGRAM AT 1.03:1, NOT A WEDGE. The render at 1.10:1 and 1.08:1 therefore MATCHES the drawing, and the previous rejection reason was a mis-measurement.

DO NOT ADD A WEDGE TAPER ON ANY FUTURE PASS - it would move the render away from the blueprint. This is the second time this session that a rigorous re-measurement has overturned an earlier eyeballed one; the first was slant-25-stripe's invented centimetre figures.

NOT measurable: the true side seam position, since this is a straight-on shot of a body and the seam wraps behind the silhouette, so all outboard clearances carry a few percent of uncertainty. Also not measurable: whether the jet under the flap is a true double besom, because the flap covers it.
